meta.title: The Lost & Found Line
meta.description: Curated records of hardware NASA (and its predecessors) left behind in Earth orbit, on the Moon, on Mars, and in deep space.

conventions.coordinates: Planetocentric latitude, east-positive longitude in degrees (0 to 360 on Mars, -180 to 180 on the Moon).
conventions.imageMatch: Regular expression tested against an archive result's title, keywords and description to drop off-topic photos.
conventions.approx: true when the published position is a landing site or an estimate rather than the object's exact resting point.
conventions.site: Short place name shown on the map marker before the item is claimed.

apis.horizons: https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/api/horizons.api (no CORS; snapshot via scripts/fetch-ephemeris.mjs into data/ephemeris.json)

route.name: Earth Orbit
route.announcement: First stop, low Earth orbit. Mind the gap between you and the oldest satellite still up here.

route.name: The Moon
route.announcement: Now arriving at the Moon. Three missions left something behind on this side.

route.name: Mars
route.announcement: Mars, all change. Six machines are parked here, and none of them are coming home.

route.name: Deep Space
route.announcement: Final stretch. Past here there are no more stations, only the two that kept going.

items.name: Vanguard 1
facts: Satellite to run on solar power
claimTag: Small enough to hold in two hands
Six antennas, no engine
Older than NASA's own logo
items.story: The oldest human-made object still in orbit. It stopped talking in 1964 but its orbit is so high that it should keep circling for centuries.
items.note: Built by the U.S. Naval Research Laboratory. Project Vanguard was transferred to NASA when the agency was founded in 1958.

sources.title: Vanguard 1 (Wikipedia)
Astronomy: Earth's oldest artificial satellite that's still in orbit

items.name: Apollo 11 Laser Ranging Retroreflector
facts: Measuring the Earth–Moon distance by laser
claimTag: Has no power and needs none
One hundred mirrors facing home
Observatories still aim lasers at it
items.story: Most of what Apollo 11 left behind is junk. This is the exception: a passive mirror array that observatories still bounce lasers off, which is how we know the Moon drifts about 3.8 cm farther away each year.

sources.title: JPL: Apollo 11 experiment still going strong after 35 years
Apollo Lunar Surface Journal: site coordinates

items.name: Surveyor 3
facts: TV camera, scoop, cables and tubing
claimTag: Had visitors two and a half years after it landed
Is missing its camera
Three legs, parked on a crater wall
items.story: The only robot on the Moon that humans went back to see. Pete Conrad landed Apollo 12 within walking distance, and he and Alan Bean cut parts off it to study how hardware ages on the lunar surface.

myth.claim: Earth bacteria survived two and a half years on the Moon inside Surveyor 3's camera.
myth.truth: Streptococcus was found in the returned camera, but later reviews point to contamination after it came back to Earth.

sources.title: JPL: Surveyor 3 camera returned from the Moon
Space.com: where are the Surveyor 3 parts retrieved by Apollo 12?

items.name: Lunar Roving Vehicle (Apollo 17)
claimTag: Four wheels made of woven wire
Last parked by the last person on the Moon
Its camera filmed the crew leaving
items.story: The crew parked it so its TV camera could film their lift-off. It is the last of the three rovers driven on the Moon, and nobody has driven anything there since.

sources.title: NASA: Apollo 17
NSSDC: Apollo landing site coordinates

items.name: Viking 1 Lander
facts: U.S. spacecraft to land and work on Mars
claimTag: Landed seven years to the day after Apollo 11
Searched the soil for life
Lost because of one wrong command
items.story: Viking 1 sent back the first clear photos from the surface of Mars and ran for more than six years. It went silent after a software update accidentally overwrote the code that pointed its antenna at Earth.

sources.title: NASA Science: Viking 1
JPL: attempts to communicate with Viking Lander 1 concluded

items.name: Sojourner
claimTag: About the size of a microwave oven
The first wheels to roll on another planet
Talked to Earth through its lander
items.story: The first rover on another planet. It was planned to last a week and kept working for nearly three months, until its lander and radio link went quiet.

sources.title: NASA Science: Mars Pathfinder

items.name: Spirit

location.label: Troy, west of Home Plate, Gusev crater

claimTag: Drove backwards for years on a broken wheel
Got stuck in soft sand
Opportunity's twin
items.story: Spirit dragged a dead front wheel for years. The furrow it dug turned up nearly pure silica, a sign of ancient hot springs. Then it bogged down in soft sand at a place called Troy and spent its last winter there.

sources.title: NASA Science: Mars Exploration Rover Spirit
NASA Technical Reports: Spirit end of mission

items.name: Opportunity
claimTag: Planned for 90 days, lasted almost 15 years
Drove farther than a marathon
Lost to a planet-wide dust storm
items.story: A 90-day mission that ran for almost fifteen years and drove more than a marathon. A global dust storm blotted out the Sun over its solar panels in June 2018, and it never woke up.

myth.claim: Opportunity's last words were "My battery is low and it's getting dark."
myth.truth: That line is a reporter's poetic summary. The real final downlink was engineering data showing almost no power and a very dark sky.

sources.title: NASA Science: Mars Exploration Rovers Spirit and Opportunity
Snopes: Opportunity's final words

items.name: InSight
claimTag: Listened to the inside of a planet
Had a seismometer under a dome
Ran out of power slowly, one dust layer at a time
items.story: InSight sat in one place and listened. Its seismometer recorded 1,319 marsquakes, including meteoroid impacts, and mapped the planet's crust, mantle and core before dust slowly choked its solar panels.

sources.title: NASA: InSight's final location on Mars
Astronomy: NASA pulls plug on Mars InSight lander

items.name: Ingenuity
claimTag: Planned for 5 flights, made 72
Broke its rotor blades on its last landing
Its resting place is named after Tolkien's Undying Lands
items.story: The first aircraft to fly on another planet. It was supposed to make five test hops and instead made 72 flights. On flight 72 it lost track of the featureless sand, damaged its rotors on landing and stayed where it came down.

sources.title: JPL: Ingenuity's flight map, 72 flights on Mars
NASA Science: farewell to our flying friend

items.name: Pioneer 10
facts: To cross the asteroid belt and fly past Jupiter
Aldebaran, in about two million years
claimTag: Carries a picture of us on a gold plaque
Its last signal came from about 12 billion km away
Going to Aldebaran, very slowly
items.story: Pioneer 10 showed that a spacecraft could cross the asteroid belt and survive Jupiter. Its last faint signal came in 2003. It still carries a plaque showing who sent it and where from.

sources.title: NASA Science: Pioneer 10
NASA Science: Pioneer 10 sends last signal

items.name: Voyager 1
claimTag: Not lost. Still answering.
A message to it takes a whole day
Carries a golden record of Earth's sounds
items.story: Voyager 1 is not abandoned. It is the farthest human-made object and it still answers. On November 18, 2026 it becomes the first one a full light-day away: a command sent from Earth takes 24 hours to reach it.

sources.title: NASA SVS: Voyager 1 one light-day visualization
CNN: Voyager 1 will reach one light-day from Earth in 2026
